title: Company Operations Reference: Access, Change, Data, Procurement & Travel
author: Nina Alvarez
body:
Overview

This consolidated reference describes company-wide policies and standardized procedures for access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor lifecycle, travel, and the canonical internal templates used across Redwood Inference. The goal is to provide a single, practical playbook teams can follow for consistent, auditable operations.

Quick links
- Access request form: /confluence/policies-and-process/templates/access-request-template
- Change request (CR) form: /confluence/policies-and-process/templates/change-request-template
- Vendor intake checklist: /confluence/policies-and-process/templates/vendor-onboarding-checklist
- Expense claim template: /confluence/policies-and-process/templates/expense-claim-form

1) Access & Permissions

Summary: Role-based access is required for all systems that contain company data. Access should be least privilege and use short-lived credentials where possible.

Key roles and ownership:
- Access owner (per system): the engineering/product/security manager who approves access and is responsible for periodic attestation.
- Identity & Access team: implements RBAC and provisioning automation.
- Requestor: the employee or manager who initiates the request.

Access request workflow (standard)
1. Requestor files an access request using the Access Request Template and selects the target system/service and requested role.
2. Access owner reviews (SLR: 3 business days). If approved, Identity & Access automation provisions access; otherwise, request returns for clarification.
3. Provisioning triggers an automated email to requestor and owner with granted permissions and expiry.
4. Quarterly attestation: owners must attest to active users; deprovisioning occurs for stale accounts.

Emergency access (break-glass)
- Use the Emergency Access channel in the Console with justification and duration.
- Emergency approvals: must be provided by an oncall engineer and a security lead. Duration default: 4 hours; extensions require written follow-up and post-event review.

Access SLA and thresholds
| Type | Max review time | Provisioning target | Renewal cadence |
|------|------------------|--------------------|------------------|
| Standard | 3 business days | 1 business day after approval | Quarterly attestation |
| Elevated (requires manager+owner) | 2 business days | Same day where possible | Monthly attestation |
| Emergency | 4 hours (approval) | Immediate | After-action review |

2) Change Management

Purpose: Ensure controlled, auditable changes to production systems and configuration with minimal customer impact.

Change categories:
- Routine: low-risk config changes with automated rollback. Can be implemented by oncall or platform engineers during business hours.
- Standard: planned changes requiring owner sign-off and automated validation (e.g., model variant rollouts).
- Major: changes with potential user impact (schema migrations, infra upgrades) requiring CAB review and a rollback plan.
- Emergency: immediate mitigation required (security incidents); follow Emergency Change process.

Change request process
1. Submit Change Request (CR) with description, rollback plan, test plan, stakeholders, and blast radius. Attach runbooks or monitoring queries.
2. Triage: Change Coordinator categorizes the CR within 24 hours.
3. Approval gates:
   - Routine: owner approval.
   - Standard: owner + 1 peer approval.
   - Major: owner + CAB approval (minimum 3 cross-functional reviewers: infra, SRE, product). CAB meeting scheduled at least 5 business days ahead.
4. Schedule: changes are scheduled in maintenance windows where feasible; major changes must include pre- and post-change verification steps.
5. Post-change: owner publishes a short status note to the change log and updates the DR/rollback artifacts.

Emergency change procedures
1. Mark CR as Emergency and notify oncall and security.
2. Implement mitigation following the emergency runbook; document all steps in the CR.
3. Complete a post-mortem within 5 business days if customer impact occurred.

Change metrics to monitor:
- % of successful changes (target > 98%)
- Mean time to approve (target < 48 hours for non-emergency)
- Number of emergency changes per quarter (target < 5)

3) Data Management & Classification

Principles: Classify data early, limit exposure, and encrypt in transit and at rest. Data ownership and retention schedules must be declared when datasets are created.

Data classification levels
- PUBLIC: Information intended for public consumption (marketing collateral, public blog posts). No special controls.
- INTERNAL: Operational data for employees (internal docs, non-sensitive telemetry). Access by default for employees but limited for some subsystems.
- CONFIDENTIAL: Customer data, security metrics, tokenized logs, non-public financials. Requires RBAC and encryption; restricted to need-to-know.
- RESTRICTED: Regulated data (PII with regulatory constraints, health data, or data under contractual restrictions). Additional controls: data processing agreements, dedicated logging, and audit trails.

Retention and deletion
- Default retention: 3 years for INTERNAL, 7 years for CONFIDENTIAL unless contractually specified, 10+ years for RESTRICTED where law requires.
- When retiring a dataset, owners must publish a deletion plan and evidence of secure wipe.

Data access requests and logs
- All access to CONFIDENTIAL and RESTRICTED datasets must be logged and reviewed monthly.
- Data access requests require a documented business justification and periodic re-attestation.

4) Procurement & Expense Controls

Approval matrix
| Amount (USD) | Required approver(s) | Notes |
|--------------|----------------------|-------|
| < 2,000 | Team lead | Routine purchases (software subscriptions under team budget) |
| 2,000 - 25,000 | Finance manager + Dept head | Requires cost justification and vendor review |
| 25,000 - 250,000 | Finance director + Legal (contract review) | Multi-year commitments require total cost of ownership (TCO) analysis |
| > 250,000 | CFO + CEO | Board notification if strategic or long-term capital commit |

Procurement steps (high level)
1. Complete Procurement Request Form (attach quotes and SOWs).
2. Finance performs vendor risk and spend categorization.
3. Legal reviews contracts and negotiates DPAs where data is involved.
4. Procurement issues PO and notifies vendor onboarding team.

Corporate card & expenses
- Monthly limits: default $3,000/month per card, adjustable with manager approval.
- Receipts: required for all transactions over $25.
- Expense submission window: within 60 days of transaction. Finance processes reimbursements bi-weekly.

Expense audit and enforcement
- Random audits quarterly covering ~5% of expense reports.
- Policy violations: first occurrence — reminder and coaching; repeat — card restrictions and HR escalation.

5) Vendor Management Lifecycle

Stages and required artifacts:
- Intake: business case, vendor questionnaire, and initial security self-attestation.
- Risk assessment: finance and security assign vendor a risk tier (Low/Medium/High). High-risk vendors require SOC2 or equivalent, penetration test results, and DPA.
- Contracting: legal owns contracts, must include SLA terms, liability limits, and data-processing clauses for any data transfer.
- Onboarding: technical integration checklist, contact matrix, and playbook for incident escalation.
- Ongoing monitoring: quarterly vendor health reviews for high-risk vendors; annual reviews for medium-risk.
- Offboarding: revoke all credentials, secure-delete shared data, and confirm contractual termination obligations.

Vendor security & privacy guardrails
- No production data in vendor test environments unless a DPA and explicit approval exist.
- Vendors with access to CONFIDENTIAL/RESTRICTED data must support logging and provide penetration test evidence within the last 12 months.

6) Travel Policy (Domestic & International)

Booking & approvals
- Employees should use the corporate travel portal for flights and hotels where available. Deviations require manager pre-approval.
- International travel to restricted geographies requires Security review and an emergency contact plan.

Expense allowances
- Domestic per diem for meals: $75/day.
- International per diem: by-country rate published in the Travel Rates spreadsheet under templates.
- Ground transportation: rideshares preferred; taxis allowed with receipts. Car rentals: compact or midsize unless pre-approved.

Health, safety & emergency
- Register international trips with People Ops and provide itinerary and local emergency contacts.
- For travel incidents: raise an incident with Security and notify manager immediately.

Reimbursement process
1. Submit expense report with receipts via Expense Claim Template within 30 days.
2. Manager approves within 5 business days.
3. Finance processes reimbursement on the next payroll run.

7) Templates & Record Locations

Canonical templates live under: /confluence/policies-and-process/templates/
- access-request-template (FORM)
- change-request-template (DOC)
- procurement-request-form (SPREADSHEET)
- vendor-onboarding-checklist (CHECKLIST)
- expense-claim-form (FORM)

Audit, reporting, and retention
- Finance/Legal keep procurement and contracting records for a minimum of 7 years. Security retains vendor security evidence for 3 years. Change logs and production access attestations retained for 5 years.

8) Exceptions, Escalations & Governance

Exceptions process
1. Submit an Exceptions Request with business justification, risk mitigations, and expiration date.
2. Risk committee reviews within 10 business days.
3. Approved exceptions are logged with a named owner and an expiry date; all exceptions are reviewed quarterly.

Escalation paths
- Access incidents: Identity & Access -> Security -> CTO for unresolved critical issues.
- Procurement disputes: Procurement -> Finance director -> CFO.
- Vendor incidents: Vendor owner -> Security -> Legal.

Governance cadence
- Monthly Ops Review: cross-functional owners review open CRs, vendor risks, procurement backlog, and outstanding exceptions.
- Quarterly Policy Review: policy owners refresh content, update thresholds, and publish change notes.

Appendix A — Example procurement justification (text)
- Business need: Expand Redis cluster to support Dedicated capacity billing aggregation.
- Options considered: cloud-managed Redis vs. self-hosted; chosen: managed for uptime and team velocity.
- Cost summary: annual license $48,000 + integration $6,000.
- Risk and mitigations: vendor SOC2 Type II, read-only access for third parties, encryption at rest and in transit.
